title: Urban infrastructure and airport access
problem: A regional government wants to understand how a proposed airport and its access network could interact with travel demand, congestion, land use, environmental pressure and unequal access. The agent must establish the geography, alternatives, time horizon and evidence before selecting model families.
decision_or_estimation_target: Estimate plausible demand and access outcomes, compare supplied alternatives and identify observations that could reverse their ranking. An exploratory intervention comparison does not establish site feasibility.
representations: Typed transport, population and land-use entities with spatial and temporal alignment
A network/accessibility model coupled to a demand or behavioral model when evidence supports that coupling
Environmental constraints and uncertain exogenous scenarios with distinct provenance
required_inputs: Candidate footprints and access proposals with source, coordinate system and date
Observed travel times, counts, origin-destination or survey information and missingness
Population, land use, environmental observations and actual planning constraints
User judgments about access, cost, distributional effects and acceptable uncertainty
compute_requirements: Network and time-series profiling; probe graph/numerical libraries in the execution environment
Paired stochastic demand scenarios, rival mechanism comparisons and sensitivity tests
SUMO/TraCI or another calibrated traffic backend only after adapter and input validation
validation_requirements: Coordinate, time, unit and population-denominator consistency
Baseline travel-time/flow reproduction and independent temporal or geographic assessment
Conservation and numerical checks; uncertainty about behavior separated from random traffic variation
Independent environmental and engineering review before feasibility conclusions
visualizations: Source-linked access maps and network diagrams
Demand/traffic trajectories with the meaning of each uncertainty range
Alternative comparison by outcome and affected group
Model-coupling and evidence-gap views
current_scope: Generic agent framing, system contracts, evidence synthesis and bounded hosted Python can investigate supplied inputs and produce conditional comparisons. This brief contains no chosen site, precomputed forecast or installed traffic simulator claim.
dependency_gaps: Local evidence and explicit candidate definitions must be supplied or acquired through admitted connectors
OSMnx/SUMO adapters and specialist simulator execution require implementation and capability checks
Engineering feasibility and causal policy effects require additional validation

title: Cellular responses and enzyme-deficiency research
problem: A research team wants to compare explanations of cellular responses, including an enzyme-deficiency extension when relevant. The agent must distinguish pathway, cellular and organismal scales and identify evidence needed to justify any connection between them.
decision_or_estimation_target: Compare mechanistic hypotheses, estimate uncertainty where parameters are identifiable and identify a discriminating validation target. The output is a research model and evidence assessment, not medical advice or a treatment/protein-design instruction.
representations: Semantic pathway and observation model with measured, latent and assumed quantities
Reaction-network or compartment dynamics with explicit conservation assumptions
An observation/error model and, where justified, cross-scale coupling to recovery outcomes
required_inputs: Published models, provenance, assay or observational data and their measurement limits
Declared biological scale, perturbation context, time horizon and recovery endpoint
Parameter units, uncertainty, missingness and population applicability
Independent research evidence for proposed cross-scale mechanisms
compute_requirements: Reproduce an admitted reference model before interpreting changes
Probe numerical solvers; compare rival dynamics, parameter identifiability and sensitivity
Use SBML/SED-ML-compatible or molecular backends only when actually available and appropriate
validation_requirements: Model provenance, units, mass balance, solver tolerances and convergence
Separate model reproduction from independent biological validation
Distinguish parameter uncertainty, structural discrepancy and measurement noise
Do not infer organism-level efficacy or resilience from a structure or synthetic trajectory
visualizations: Pathway and cross-scale hypothesis graphs
Observed versus modeled response with source and basis labels
Sensitivity and identifiability diagnostics
Optional structure viewer for an admitted structure, separate from functional claims
current_scope: The generic engine can frame the research, synthesize supplied evidence and execute exploratory numerical models with explicit assumptions. No enzyme intervention, molecular design or clinically valid result is precomputed.
dependency_gaps: Suitable reference models and independent biological evidence are required
OpenMM was unavailable in the recorded hosted probe; a specialist adapter is required
SBML/SED-ML execution and cross-scale validity must be checked for the selected model

title: Prediction markets and event uncertainty
problem: An analyst wants to understand whether market-implied probabilities and evidence-based forecasts reliably describe a precisely defined set of events. The agent must reconcile settlement semantics, event dependence, source availability and rival forecasting explanations before computing comparisons.
decision_or_estimation_target: Estimate event uncertainty, compare forecasts with raw-price and simple reference baselines, and assess calibration where independent outcomes exist. Market creation, demand estimation, optimization, reinforcement learning and mechanism design remain future extensions.
representations: Events, settlement rules, thresholds and first-availability times in a semantic contract
Probabilistic temporal or hierarchical forecasts with explicit event dependencies
A source and market-observation process separated from the latent event outcome
required_inputs: Forecast or market snapshots with settlement definitions, observation and availability timestamps
Resolved outcomes, event-group identities and the intended forecast cutoff
Source-linked evidence and definition changes with point-in-time provenance
Market coverage, missingness and relevant economic context with vintage
compute_requirements: Semantic admission, timestamp checks and simple reference forecasts before added model complexity
Probabilistic estimation, prediction checks and sensitivity to missing or dependent events
Probe PyMC or other selected inference libraries before requesting their use
validation_requirements: Temporal holdout and availability checks with dependent contracts kept in the same event group
Compare the same eligible forecasts using a frozen proper scoring rule and reference baseline
Check calibration only on eligible independent outcomes and report sampling limits
Retain unresolved settlement-definition, selection and source-dependence uncertainty
visualizations: Forecast trajectories with evidence and resolution timelines
Reliability and proper-score comparisons where observed outcomes support them
Competing model comparisons with data and assumption lineage
Evidence gaps and the next discriminating measurement
current_scope: Generic framing, evidence synthesis and bounded hosted inference over supplied data. The narrow prepared P1 adapter supplies semantic admission and host scoring for eligible threshold-event packs; broader markets require new admitted contracts. No forecast, investment recommendation or market mechanism is precomputed.
dependency_gaps: A real point-in-time forecast archive with settlement rules and independent outcomes is needed
PyMC availability must be confirmed in the selected execution environment
Market-platform and World Bank acquisition still need admitted scoped connectors
Market creation, demand estimation, optimization, reinforcement learning and mechanism design are future extensions

title: Geopolitical and economic exposure
problem: An analyst wants to understand possible political, economic and humanitarian developments across a defined region and horizon. The agent must distinguish reported events, source coverage, delayed coding, strategic assumptions and rival scenario mechanisms.
decision_or_estimation_target: Produce scoped scenario or forecast comparisons, identify leading uncertainties and state which observations would change the assessment. This is strategic analysis, without tactical military planning or targeting.
representations: Versioned actor, institution, event and economic dependency graphs
A source/reporting process separated from latent real-world events
Probabilistic temporal or scenario models with explicit rival mechanisms
required_inputs: Defined region, horizon, outcomes and decision context
Versioned event data, original source references and publication/availability timestamps
Economic and institutional indicators with definition changes recorded
User judgments and scenario assumptions separated from empirical evidence
compute_requirements: Entity reconciliation, duplicate/reporting-dependence inspection and temporal alignment
Baseline forecasts, retrospective evaluation and conditional scenario sensitivity
Bounded graph/probabilistic computation with unavailable data recorded as gaps
validation_requirements: Point-in-time availability and no retrospective knowledge leakage
Holdouts by time or event family with dependency-aware comparisons
Document reporting bias, changing definitions and unresolved source disagreement
No scenario probability without a stated estimation and calibration basis
visualizations: Source-linked event timelines and actor/dependency graphs
Scenario branches with observable triggers
Forecast verification and disagreement views
Optional coarse spatial summaries for the stated analytical scope
current_scope: The engine can synthesize evidence, represent rival explanations and compute exploratory comparisons from admitted data. This is an investigation brief, not a precomputed forecast or a tactical system.
dependency_gaps: UCDP API access requires a requested token and versioned acquisition adapter
GDELT and World Bank connectors are not currently installed as domain adapters
News mentions are not independent ground-truth events; source assessment remains necessary

title: Climate, agriculture and ecological systems
problem: A team wants to understand how climate drivers, water, ecological dynamics and human activities interact. A Hudson River ecology/community investigation is one concrete example; an agricultural question may instead require soil, crop and management observations. The agent must establish relevant spatial, seasonal and social scales before choosing mechanisms.
decision_or_estimation_target: Estimate and compare ecological, water-state or agricultural outcomes, test plausible coupling mechanisms and identify missing observations. The Hudson example connects river state and community exposure; exploratory interventions remain conditional on the selected model and evidence.
representations: Climate and hydrological states coupled to ecological, crop or human-use observations as relevant
Spatial units, monitoring stations, communities and shared reference clocks; river reaches for the Hudson example
Mechanistic or stochastic dynamics with an explicit sensor and reporting process
required_inputs: Weather, water-quality or flow observations with station metadata, QA flags and units
River geometry, temporal support, tidal or seasonal context and source provenance
Ecological or soil/crop observations and aggregate human-use/exposure data at compatible scales
User priorities and proposed actions, clearly separated from measured effects
compute_requirements: Station/time alignment, missingness inspection and quality-control-aware profiling
Probe numerical and labeled-array tools; compare rival state/observation models
Replicated scenarios, conservation checks and uncertainty propagation across couplings
validation_requirements: Sensor calibration and QA flags, unit consistency and valid temporal aggregation
Seasonal and station holdouts; dependence among nearby sensors retained
Mass balance and numerical stability where implied by the selected model
Do not infer community exposure or causal ecological change from a single proxy
visualizations: Source-linked station/reach maps and ecological/social coupling graphs
Aligned river and weather time series with QA/missingness overlays
Model/data comparisons and seasonal uncertainty
Community-level trade-offs and discriminating evidence gaps
current_scope: The generic engine can work with supplied monitoring exports, synthesize source disagreements and create scoped model comparisons. HRECOS/USGS are resource candidates for the Hudson example, not agricultural datasets. No calibrated ecosystem/crop model, ecological conclusion or public-health recommendation is preloaded.
dependency_gaps: HRECOS offers live views and a data-request path; bulk records have not been acquired
USGS OGC/STAC acquisition and xarray integration require scoped adapters and capability checks
A hydrodynamic, ecological or crop specialist backend and case-specific data may be needed beyond exploratory Python
Social and ecological measurements require compatible scale and provenance

title: City population and social dynamics
problem: A city team wants to understand how population change, housing, mobility, services and heterogeneous behavior interact. The agent must decide which mechanisms and scales are necessary, using aggregate evidence and explicitly labeled synthetic populations where appropriate.
decision_or_estimation_target: Estimate population/service-demand outcomes and compare model explanations or supplied scenarios. A 3D scene should help inspect computed results, not manufacture realism or imply individual-level prediction.
representations: Cohorts, neighborhoods, households or synthetic agents with declared aggregation rules
Demographic state transitions coupled to housing, mobility or service-demand mechanisms
Network or agent-based behavior only when its assumptions and observations are explicit
required_inputs: Population, housing and social estimates with survey uncertainty and geographic vintage
Aggregate flows, service observations and land-use geometry with units and dates
Behavioral evidence, transition assumptions and synthetic-population construction provenance
User-selected outcomes, comparison horizon and distributional priorities
compute_requirements: Baseline cohort or flow model before introducing heterogeneous-agent complexity
Replicated simulations with declared schedules, seeds and sampling assumptions
Mesa or another ABM backend requires actual availability; 3D rendering is a separate adapter
validation_requirements: Population accounting, unit/time alignment and plausible transition bounds
Validate aggregate and subgroup observables against independent evidence
Sensitivity to behavioral rules and update order; preserve model disagreement
Keep simulated agents distinct from observed people and illustrative geometry distinct from surveys
visualizations: Cohort/population flow diagrams and subgroup trajectories
Neighborhood comparison maps with uncertainty and data vintage
Optional 3D extrusions or movement playback derived from admitted geometry and computed outputs
Behavioral assumptions, model diagnostics and evidence lineage
current_scope: Agent framing, typed system representation, evidence synthesis and bounded hosted computation over supplied inputs. Advanced 3D rendering and a calibrated city ABM are extension targets, not installed capabilities or precomputed simulations.
dependency_gaps: Census API queries require a key; geography/vintage mapping and an acquisition adapter are needed
Mesa was unavailable in the recorded hosted probe
deck.gl/3D scene integration is not installed in the current frontend
Behavioral calibration and independent city-specific evidence are required
